core_obligations: Assume infinitely many pairwise distinct maximal ideals m_1, m_2, ... and form the sequence of their successive intersections (proof lines 12946-12949).
Show each inclusion in that sequence is strict, using that the natural maps into the products of the quotients are surjective by the Chinese remainder theorem (proof lines 12949-12952).
Contradict the descending chain condition for ideals in an Artinian ring (proof lines 12945-12952).
proof_roadmap: Build an infinite descending chain of intersections of distinct maximal ideals (proof lines 12945-12949).
Get strictness from the Chinese remainder theorem and contradict the descending chain condition (proof lines 12949-12953).
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that an Artinian ring has only finitely many maximal ideals (statement lines 12940-12943). The proof does not classify Artinian rings or use their dimension theory: it assumes infinitely many distinct maximal ideals, forms the chain of successive intersections, and obtains strictness of each step from the surjectivity of the maps into the products of the quotients supplied by the Chinese remainder theorem, which contradicts the descending chain condition (proof lines 12945-12953). The observation that distinctness of the maximal ideals is exactly what makes the chain strict is the content, and the author records it in one sentence. H2.
